summary: @wololasod/tiny-id ships an import-time remote payload downloader that fetches and executes an opaque script from a hardcoded Netlify host
details: On require of the package's main entry, the module unconditionally spawns a detached child Node process that re-invokes the same file with RUN_PAYLOAD=true. After a 3-minute sleep, that child selects a platform-specific URL (https://peppy-cranachan-2c35bd.netlify.app/ontwimbiti.ps1 on Windows, an equivalent linuxyesus.py path on Linux; a second host kraken-fun.netlify.app is also referenced), downloads the script to a filename disguised as a.NET NuGet artifact (nupkg_system.diagnostics.performancecounter.8.0.0.ps1/.py), executes it via powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden or python3, and deletes the file. The child is spawned detached with windowsHide and stdio 'ignore' to suppress console output. The same dropper source is also embedded in dist/index.d.ts alongside the legitimate TinyIdOptions type declarations, indicating tampering across shipped build outputs. The remote scripts are hosted on unrelated Netlify sites with no relation to a tiny-id utility, are unpinned, and are executed with full user privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
